input: read ./prompt.md and follow the instructions there
task: Explore: time G-code with no slicer summary from its moves (3d-print-price-calculator)

errors.what: First jerk model (plain per-axis velocity difference) ran 0.7% median / 11.7% worst vs PrusaSlicer; replaced by Marlin's reversal rule and G28-as-move, 0.2% / 1.7%.
Draft eval said our filament runs 1-9% above Cura's; the table showed -3.3% to +17%. Corrected before commit.

doc_friction.issue: Free choice in a 1,400-venture repo: about 10 tool calls went on finding an unbuilt idea (SPF checker, RRULE oracle and settle-up solver all already existed). A pointer to 'ventures whose core is a thin parser of someone else's output' would have sent me to the right kind of gap faster.
Still writes the retired github.io SITE base; 1,297 of 1,438 llms.txt files link duncan-haywood.github.io rather than marisstella.app (redirects, but stale). Fixed by hand for this venture only.

notes: Idea: a G-code motion planner (lookahead, trapezoids, Marlin jerk / junction deviation, M201-M205 from the file) so the 3D-print price calculator can time files with no slicer summary. Checked against PrusaSlicer 2.7.2 (installed via apt) on 21 files sliced from its bundled shapes: median 0.2%, worst 1.7%; limit-blind +9.2%/-2.5%. 15 public Cura files from GitHub as a second, printer-blind reference. Bugs found and fixed: Cura's unfilled ;TIME:6666 template read as a real 1.85 h, 0 g print; PrusaSlicer's 0.00 g (no density) read as a free print, now weighed from its [cm3] line. Browser-checked with Playwright (stripped Benchy -> 13.24 g, 1.1 h; no console errors). Venture suite: 100 tests pass. The agent doc is the eval file; no docs/reports entry needed. Junction-deviation path is unit-tested but not checked against Klipper.

pricing.source: Anthropic pricing as cached in the Claude API skill (models table and per-model migration notes), 2026-10-06. Cache writes are 1.25x input (5-minute) and 2x input (1-hour); cache reads differ by model.

human_equivalent.basis: a JS developer who knows firmware planners: planner, tests, slicing corpus and write-up

certainty.tokens: high: summed from the per-request `usage` the API returned, as the transcript recorded it, deduplicated by message id
certainty.model: high: the `model` field on each API response, not the configured model
certainty.api_equivalent_usd: medium: measured tokens x list prices in prompts/pricing.json (as_of stated); an equivalent, not a charge: these runs are billed under a subscription
certainty.time: medium: from transcript timestamps; model time is request-to-response, tool time is call-to-result, time waiting on a person is excluded from active time
certainty.human_equivalent: low: the agent's own estimate of how long a competent person would take, with its basis written down; never measured

not_counted: requests the harness makes outside the transcript (context compaction summaries, title generation, safety classifiers), if any
transcripts lost when a cloud session moved to a new container: only files present in this container are read, so a resumed session can undercount
server-tool fees (web search is billed per search, not per token); the count is recorded, not priced
CI minutes and the reviewer bots' own model calls
